feedback.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| & =4\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{4+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-4|\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot {C}_{21}+0\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(9-2) \\  & =-14\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|=-4\cdot (-14)=56.
$$
